blocking.issue: Row 2 already charges all of R per attempt, but per-attempt settlement is one of the amendments OQ-ai-llm-gateway-15 proposes. The document says OQ-15's other proposals do not apply before it closes, so it applies one pending proposal now and defers the others. Pack 8.9 charges all of R once, since R is the single reservation for the request. Charging per attempt multiplies that charge. A request can make up to (retries.attempts + 1) x candidates attempts, and every 5xx, 429 or perTryTimeout attempt that reaches a provider charges another R, even though the provider bills nothing for most of them. During a provider brownout, a Consumer's daily Token Budget can drain several times faster than its real usage. The Gateway then returns RZ-AI-006 for the rest of the window, so an upstream fault becomes a client-side denial.
blocking.evidence: Line 316: "`onLog` settles asynchronously, one cost record per attempt. Rows 1 and 2 apply pack 8.9, row 2 per attempt:". Line 321: "| Attempt reached the provider, no usage read | Error status, `perTryTimeout`, stream error, interruption, client disconnect before or after commit, `RZ-AI-013` | All of R for that attempt | ...". Line 324: "OQ-ai-llm-gateway-15 also proposes charging nothing for error statuses and the larger of R and partial provider usage for interruptions; neither applies before it closes." Line 617 (OQ-15): "... a guard tolerance above C, per-attempt settlement, release of R without an attempt ...". Line 206: "a request makes at most (`retries.attempts` + 1) x candidates attempts". Pack 8.9: "When usage is missing (interrupted stream, no usage reported), charge all of R".
blocking.fix: Settle per request until OQ-15 closes. Change line 316 to "`onLog` settles asynchronously, one cost record per attempt; rows 1 and 2 apply pack 8.9 per request:". Change the row 2 Charge cell to "All of R once per request, plus usage other attempts reported". Keep the per-attempt `ruralz_ai_usage_missing_total` signal. OQ-15 already lists per-attempt settlement, so no OQ text changes. The fix is about word-neutral; the body is at 4,981 of 5,000 words.

blocking.issue: The round-1 fix removed the prompt-size bound from the 1 ms p99 target for Gateway-added time to first token. The target now covers any request up to maxRequestBodyBytes. That work includes a strict full parse that finds repeated member names at any depth after unescaping, plus façade decode and re-encode or in-place edits. None of that is excluded, and all of it grows linearly with body size. A strict JSON parse of a request body of several hundred KiB to several MiB cannot finish in 1 ms. That is common for RAG or long-context requests. As written, the target is implausible and no benchmark can confirm it. Only estimator time was split out as a per-KiB cost.
blocking.evidence: Line 126: "Gateway-added time to first token, excluding State Store, embedding, provider and estimator time: 1 ms or less at p99 (target). Estimator time is a per-KiB cost (hypothesis) that an M3 benchmark of `tiktoken-go/tokenizer` measures". Line 99: "Every `request.body` decode that CEL, a Policy or the decoder reads MUST reject invalid UTF-8 and repeated member names at any depth, compared after unescaping". Line 103: "It decodes the body into one internal form, encodes it for the candidate's dialect".
blocking.fix: Put a size bound back and make the size-dependent work a per-KiB cost. Replace line 126 with: "Gateway-added time to first token for bodies up to 16 KiB, excluding State Store, embedding, provider and estimator time: 1 ms or less at p99 (target); parsing, translation and estimation add per-KiB costs (hypothesis) that an M3 benchmark of `tiktoken-go/tokenizer` and the decoder measures ([Performance budgets and benchmarking](...))." This is about word-neutral.

non_blocking.suggestion: The body is 4,981 words by the verifier's rule, against a maximum of 5,000, so any fix that adds words will fail the band. Pay for additions by, for example, trimming the Personas paragraph or the Guarantee sentence about LiteLLM.

non_blocking.section: Token-aware rate limits and budgets (Token Budget: Keys)
non_blocking.suggestion: Settlement adjusts the reserving window, but under Traffic management a quota key expires one window after that window closes. With `window: 1m` and `timeout: 120s`, a stream that starts early in a window can settle after the key is gone. If the settlement script then writes, it recreates a counter without a TTL, and under the required `noeviction` that is a leak. State that settlement to a missing window key is a no-op counted by a metric, and never sets a key without `PEXPIRE`.

Option (c), "evict only keys with TTLs" (volatile-*), would evict Token Budget and rate-limit keys, which all carry `PEXPIRE`. Traffic management says "`noeviction` is REQUIRED" because evicting them causes silent resets and unbounded over-admission. Replace option (c) with one that is viable, such as a per-principal byte cap enforced by the store script.

non_blocking.section: Prompt caching and semantic caching (Semantic Cache: Storage)
non_blocking.suggestion: Putting all of a principal's partitions under one hash tag places all Semantic Cache traffic for a heavy single Consumer on one shard, for example an application backend that uses one API key. Note the hot-shard trade-off, and name the per-principal caps as the reason for it, in OQ-18. Also state the main-thread cost of one store script as a hypothesis: VADD plus up to 64 VREMs run synchronously inside Lua.

non_blocking.section: Prompt caching and semantic caching (Semantic Cache: Look up)
non_blocking.suggestion: On valkey-search, say that the partition is a TAG pre-filter on the per-AIModel index. Say also that in cluster mode FT.SEARCH fans out to every shard, so lookup cost grows with shard count. On Vector Sets, a timestamp FILTER may parse each visited element's JSON attributes, and each can hold up to 32 KiB of completion. Consider checking the returned element's timestamp in the Node, or keeping the timestamp outside the large attribute.

The Configuration model's tee rule already increments `ruralz_cache_store_skipped_total` for `ai.semantic-cache` store skips. The new proposal `ruralz_ai_semantic_cache_store_skipped_total` overlaps with it. Either reuse the existing counter with a `reason` label, or state how the two differ.
